rationale: TS_MIN of a pointwise MIN is algebraically identical to MIN of the two separate five-year troughs, so the advertised "within-year binding constraint" novelty is illusory and the signal reduces to a re-blend of InternallyFundedRnDFloor and TroughCashFlowInnovator, with the added defect that COALESCE(xrd,0) piles all non-R&D firms at exactly zero while loss-year firms fall below them, so the cross-section is driven by cash-flow distress rather than by research capacity.

A defensible conjunction of two independently strong archive legs whose information sets differ (five-year policy floor vs. contemporaneous restated return), though the two legs share the xrd stock and the IND_RANK-product form is by now the project's default template, so expected incremental content is modest.

R&D stock scaled by liabilities is essentially the product of two long-published effects (R&D intensity and low leverage) with no interaction beyond division, and because COALESCE(xrd,0) forces the numerator to zero for the majority of firms the industry rank collapses into a large tie block that mostly re-sorts on nothing.

Economically coherent impairment-trigger story, but it is a one-operator substitution (MA→TS_MIN) on the identical two legs of IntangibleBookWeakDebtCoverage — a cosmetic refinement of an already-tested signal rather than new content, and the trough of oancf/lt is close to a standard distress screen.

The move from a one-year leverage delta to a five-year liability-share trend is a substantive rather than cosmetic repair of SelfFinancedRnDExpansion and adds a financing-policy dimension absent from the best commitment signal, though the deleveraging leg overlaps with the well-known net-external-financing anomaly.

The stated diagnosis is selective and inconsistent with the archive — CapitalLightKnowledgeFranchise actually produced a correctly signed FF5 alpha (+2.0%, t=2.43) alongside its wrong-signed slope — so this is a bare sign flip of a mixed-evidence signal, and asserting a positive premium for high dp/at directly contradicts the established investment/asset-intensity effect without any new identifying content.
